en.html:
Lightning safety, step by step

OSHA and NOAA recommend these best practices for anyone whose job involves working outdoors. Work through each step in order.

Lightning warning systems

An EAP can include lightning warning or detection systems, but no system can detect the "first strike," detect all lightning, or predict lightning strikes. Select each tab to compare the options.

Lightning Safety When Working Outdoors

Lightning is often overlooked as an occupational hazard, yet it can severely injure or kill workers whose jobs take them outdoors. This course is based on the joint OSHA and NOAA fact sheet Lightning Safety When Working Outdoors (FS-3863).

By the end of this course you will be able to:

  • Recognize lightning as a workplace hazard and identify higher-risk jobs
  • Apply the "When thunder roars, go indoors" rule and choose safe shelter
  • Describe what a lightning safety protocol in an Emergency Action Plan must cover
  • Reduce your risk if you are caught outside in a thunderstorm
  • Explain the OSHA requirements and worker rights that apply

Who is at risk?

Workers have significant exposure to lightning when they work outdoors in open spaces, on or near tall objects, or near explosives or conductive materials such as metal. Expand each group to see the higher-risk activities.

Work on or from scaffolds is prohibited during storms or high winds (29 CFR 1926.451(f)(12)).

Work may continue only if a qualified person determines it is safe and personal fall protection or wind screens are provided.

Crane hoists are prohibited during storms or high winds (29 CFR 1926.1431(k)(8)).

Hoisting may continue only if a qualified person determines it is safe.
Work on top of walls is prohibited during storms or high winds (29 CFR 1926.854(c)).
Correct. Lightning can strike up to 10 miles from any rainfall.
The correct answer is up to 10 miles. Lightning can strike well outside the heaviest rainfall.
Not quite. Review the options and try again.

label.en: Only directly under the heaviest rain

en.html: How far from any rainfall can lightning strike?

• Roofing
  • Construction, such as scaffolding work
  • Building maintenance
  • Plumbing and pipe fitting
  • Heavy equipment operation

• Power utility field repair
  • Steel erection and telecommunications

• Logging
  • Farming and field labor
  • Lawn services and landscaping

• Airport ground personnel operations
  • Pool and beach lifeguarding
  • Explosives handling or storage

Check NOAA weather reports before outdoor work begins. Use weather.gov and radio forecasts to check for all weather hazards. Consider rescheduling jobs so workers aren't caught outside in hazardous weather.
Keep watching the weather while you work. Darkening clouds and rising wind speeds can signal a developing thunderstorm. Follow local TV, radio, and internet reports and emergency notifications.
At the first thunder or lightning, go to a designated building. Supervisors should tell workers in advance which buildings to use. Choose fully enclosed buildings with electrical wiring and plumbing.
If no safe building is available, use a hard-topped metal vehicle with the windows rolled up.
Stay sheltered for at least 30 minutes after the last thunder. Going back outside too soon is a common cause of lightning injuries.
Don't use corded phones after you hear thunder, except in an emergency. Cell phones and cordless phones are safe to use.

Lightning safety training

Employers should train all workers on lightning safety, and the training should cover each outdoor worksite. That way, supervisors and workers know in advance:

  • where the worksite's safe shelters are
  • how long it takes to reach them

Supervisors and workers should also be trained to give lightning warnings early enough for everyone to reach shelter and take other precautions.

NOAA recommends that employers rely first on NOAA weather reports, including NOAA Weather Radio All Hazards. When you need advance notice of storms, monitor forecasts and radar from NOAA or commercial weather services.

Commercial detection and notification services can send alerts when lightning develops or comes within a set range of a worksite. They can also map where strikes are landing. However, they can't predict the first strike.

Portable detectors pick up the electromagnetic signal from a nearby strike and estimate its distance. They usually miss some strikes, can't predict the first strike, and can't pinpoint where a strike landed. They are also less accurate than commercial systems.
Keep watching the sky for storms developing overhead or nearby. Sometimes listening for thunder or watching the sky warns you sooner than a detector does. Get to a safe place before the first strike.
Correct. No system can detect the first strike, and handheld detectors usually miss some strikes. Watching the sky and checking NOAA reports are still essential.
Two statements are true: no system can detect the first strike, and handheld detectors may miss strikes. No system can predict strikes, and none replaces watching the sky.
Not quite. Review the options and try again.
You found some but not all of the right answers. No system can detect the first strike, and handheld detectors may miss strikes. No system can predict where lightning will strike.
You are partly right. Look again and try once more.

What is lightning?

Lightning is a giant spark of electricity in the atmosphere, either between clouds or between a cloud and the ground. It can occur:

  • Between the cloud and the ground (cloud-to-ground lightning)
  • Within and between thunderstorm clouds (intra-cloud and inter-cloud lightning)

Many victims are caught outside because they did not act promptly to get to a safe place, or because they went back outside too soon after a storm passed.
Review your worksite's protocol. Check off each item once you have confirmed your lightning safety protocol covers it.

label.en: Tells workers to act on thunder, lightning, or other storm signs

en.html: Lightning is likely to strike the tallest object in an area. Avoid isolated tall trees, hilltops, utility poles, cell towers, cranes, large equipment, ladders, scaffolding, and rooftops.

Stay out of open areas such as fields, and never lie flat on the ground. Move to a dense stand of smaller trees surrounded by larger trees, or to low-lying ground such as a valley or ditch. Watch out for flooding.
Get out of and away from pools, lakes, and other bodies of water immediately. Water doesn't attract lightning, but it conducts electricity very well.
Avoid wiring, plumbing, and fencing. Lightning can travel long distances through metal, so stay away from all metal objects, equipment, and surfaces that can conduct electricity.
Sheds, pavilions, tents, and covered porches don't provide adequate protection from lightning.

Seek a fully enclosed, substantial building with wiring and plumbing, which act as an earth ground. Once inside, avoid contact with anything that conducts electricity: electrical equipment, cords, plumbing fixtures, and corded phones. Don't lean against concrete walls or floors, which may contain metal bars.

Emergency Action Plan

Employers should have a written Emergency Action Plan (EAP), as outlined in 29 CFR 1910.38 or 29 CFR 1926.35. The EAP should include a written lightning safety protocol for outdoor workers. Employers should also post lightning safety information at outdoor worksites and train every employee to follow the EAP.

OSHA standards

Under the General Duty Clause, Section 5(a)(1) of the Occupational Safety and Health Act of 1970, employers must provide a workplace "free from recognizable hazards that are causing or likely to cause death or serious harm to employees."

Courts have interpreted this to mean employers must address hazards the employer or industry recognizes, whenever a feasible way to reduce the hazard exists. This includes lightning hazards.
Correct. Only fully enclosed buildings with wiring and plumbing, and hard-topped metal vehicles with the windows up, give adequate protection.

en.html: During a storm, when can scaffold work continue?

When thunder roars, go indoors!

If you hear thunder, even a distant rumble, get to a safe place immediately. Thunderstorms always include lightning, and any thunder you hear is caused by lightning.

NOAA advises that nowhere outside is safe when thunderstorms are in your area. If you see signs of an approaching thunderstorm, don't begin any task you can't stop quickly.
Correct. Stay sheltered for at least 30 minutes after the last thunder you hear.
The correct answer is at least 30 minutes after the last thunder. Lightning can strike well away from rain, and going back outside too soon is a common way people get hurt.
Not quite. Review the options and try again.

label.en: Until you can no longer see lightning

en.html: You are sheltering in a building during a storm. How long should you wait after the last thunder before going back outside?

If you are caught outside

If you are caught outside in a thunderstorm, there may be nothing you can do to avoid being struck. There is no safe place outside in a thunderstorm. That is why it is so important to reach a safe place at the first sign of a storm.

If you can't get to shelter, follow NOAA's recommendations to lower your risk. Expand each topic below.
Working conditions that do not pose a risk of serious harm.
Information and training about workplace hazards, how to prevent them, and the OSHA standards that apply, in a language and vocabulary the worker understands.
Review records of work-related injuries and illnesses.
Ask OSHA to inspect the workplace if they believe there is a serious hazard or that their employer isn't following OSHA rules. OSHA keeps all identities confidential.
Exercise their rights without retaliation. A worker who faces retaliation must file a complaint with OSHA as soon as possible, and no later than 30 days after the retaliation.
Correct. Any thunder you hear is caused by lightning, so get to a safe place right away.
The correct answer is to get to a safe place immediately. When thunder roars, go indoors.
Not quite. Review the options and try again.

label.en: Get to a safe place immediately
Finish the current task, then go inside

sortingDragStartAria.de: Element aufgehoben. Es befindet sich derzeit in Position {{position}}. Verwenden Sie die Hoch- und Runter-Pfeiltasten, um es zu verschieben.
sortingDragStartAria.en: Item picked up. It is currently in position {{position}}. Use the up and down arrow keys to move it.

sortingDragStartAria.fr: Élément pris. Il est actuellement en position {{position}}. Utilisez les flèches haut et bas pour le déplacer.
sortingDragStartAria.it: Elemento preso. È attualmente in posizione {{position}}. Usa le freccie su e giù per spostarlo.
sortingDragStartAria.nl: Element opgehaald. Het bevindt zich momenteel in positie {{position}}. Gebruik de pijltoetsen om het te verplaatsen.
sortingDragStartAria.pl: Element przyjęty. Jest obecnie w pozycji {{position}}. Użyj strzałek w górę i w dół, aby przesunąć go.
sortingDragStartAria.pt-PT: Item pego. Está atualmente na posição {{position}}. Use as teclas de seta para mover.
sortingDragStartAria.ru: Элемент взят. Он находится в позиции {{position}}. Используйте стрелки вверх и вниз, чтобы переместить его.

sortingDragUpdateAria.de: Verschieben des Elements von Position {{position}} zu Position {{newPosition}}. Drücken Sie die Leertaste, um zu bestätigen, oder die Escape-Taste, um abzubrechen.
sortingDragUpdateAria.en: Moving item from position {{position}} to position {{newPosition}}. press the space bar to confirm or press the escape key to cancel.
sortingDragUpdateAria.es: Moviendo el elemento de la posición {{position}} a la posición {{newPosition}}. Presiona el espacio para confirmar o presiona la tecla escape para cancelar.
sortingDragUpdateAria.fr: Déplacement de l'élément de la position {{position}} à la position {{newPosition}}. Appuyez sur la barre d'espace pour confirmer ou appuyez sur la touche escape pour annuler.
sortingDragUpdateAria.it: Spostamento dell'elemento dalla posizione {{position}} alla posizione {{newPosition}}. Premi spazio per confermare o premi escape per annullare.
sortingDragUpdateAria.nl: Element verplaatst van positie {{position}} naar positie {{newPosition}}. Druk op spatie om te bevestigen of op escape om te annuleren.
sortingDragUpdateAria.pl: Przesuwanie elementu z pozycji {{position}} do pozycji {{newPosition}}. Naciśnij spację, aby potwierdzić, lub escape, aby anulować.
sortingDragUpdateAria.pt-PT: Movendo item da posição {{position}} para a posição {{newPosition}}. pressione o espaço para confirmar ou pressione a tecla de escape para cancelar.
sortingDragUpdateAria.ru: Перемещение элемента из позиции {{position}} в позицию {{newPosition}}. Нажмите пробел, чтобы подтвердить, или Escape, чтобы отменить.
sortingDragUpdateAria.tr: Eleman {{position}} pozisyonundan {{newPosition}} pozisyonuna taşınıyor. Boşluk tuşuna basarak onaylayın veya Escape tuşuna basarak iptal edin.
